title: Sam Parr on quitting alcohol: 6 lessons from one year sober (2014)
summary: A 2014 personal essay where Sam Parr shares what changed after a year of sobriety: fitness, confidence, clarity, and emotional control. Mostly personal reflection, with durable mindset lessons about facing stress head-on, exercise as a mood and work-ethic driver, and conviction building confidence.

principles.text: Exercise boosts mood, alertness, confidence and work ethic; skipping it makes you feel bad.
principles.quote: After working out, I felt happy, more alert, and best of all, confident. I noticed an increase in my work ethic too.

principles.text: Sticking to your convictions builds real confidence, which makes you more attractive than relying on false confidence.
principles.quote: Women like confident men and in the past I relied on booze for false confidence.

principles.text: Facing stressful, high-stakes moments clear-headed is a rush; embrace obstacles instead of numbing yourself.
principles.quote: In fact, I now embrace obstacles because I love the exhilarating emotion of feeling the stress, pain, and achievement when overcoming it.

principles.text: Starting a business is scary and stressful; feeling every emotion fully is what makes it energizing.
principles.quote: Yes, starting a new business is scary and stressful, but I felt every emotion and loved it.

principles.text: Controlling your emotions lets you step back, analyze, and decide well instead of acting impulsively.
principles.quote: When something bad happens I’m able to calmly take a step back, analyze what’s going on, how I feel, then make a proper decision

principles.text: Removing a habit that wrecks your energy frees you to commit to mornings, health and action.
principles.quote: For years I’d never commit to Saturday or Sunday morning activities because I knew I’d still be drunk or hungover in the AM.
